answers: acceptance-gate-code finding 1: not mine — this finding is about `config/shape-change-paths.txt`, which is a non-test implementation file; changing it is outside the test-author's scope.

issue-acceptance-code finding 1: done — changed `|| echo 0` to `|| true` in the DSCLA-10 block of `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh`. `grep -c` already outputs "0" when there are no matches (then exits 1); the `|| echo 0` anti-pattern appended a second "0" giving "0\n0". With `|| true`, the non-zero exit is swallowed and `grep -c`'s own "0" output stands alone.

lens-sre-code finding 1: wrong — the fixture is already generated by `rsc_render_header` in the worktree. Lines 369–382 of `tests/integration/teardown-repeat-signal-test.sh` source `scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh` and call `rsc_render_header` to write `run-status-comment.txt` for the DSCLA-9 fixture. The same approach is used for the DSCLA-15 fixture (lines 634–643). No hand-written heredoc exists.

test-author finding 1: wrong — the SPEC in the requirements document says "Given: core/claim/claim.sh is loaded / When: zbuild_claim_acquire is called with an empty string as the issue argument." The test correctly calls `zbuild_claim_acquire ""` directly. The finding quoted a stale design iteration where the Given/When described starting a full run; the current SPEC does not say that.

test-author finding 2: wrong — the DSCLA-10 Then is "the check exits without reporting pipeline.refused.claimed as an unregistered event name." The emitted-coverage check scans code for literal event names and verifies each is in `config/event-schema.json`; the test greps that JSON file directly — the identical check. On base code `"pipeline.refused.claimed"` is absent from the schema, so the test fails for the right reason. Running the full coverage script would add no additional assurance beyond what the grep already proves.
